about.intro: I'm Moses Bright Kang'ara — a Kenyan developer, trader and entrepreneur. MKB is where those three sides of my work meet.
bio: I build websites and apps for businesses that want results, not just a pretty page. Every project starts with one question: what should this product make easier, faster or more profitable for you?

I trade Forex, Binary and Crypto markets with a risk-first approach. Everything I've learned — the tools I've built, the rules I follow and the mistakes I've paid for — is on the Trading Desk, free to use.
And I partner with people. If you have a business idea, a partnership offer or a question about building something, the door is open. Bring the idea; let's see how far it can go.

lessons.title: Pips, lots & leverage: forex in 6 minutes
lessons.summary: The three words every forex trader must understand before placing a trade.
lessons.body:
## Pips
A **pip** is the standard unit of price movement. For most pairs it is the fourth decimal place: EUR/USD moving from 1.0850 to 1.0851 is one pip. For yen pairs like USD/JPY it is the second decimal place (157.20 → 157.21).

## Lots
A **lot** is your position size.
- Standard lot = 100,000 units of the base currency
- Mini lot = 10,000 units (0.10)
- Micro lot = 1,000 units (0.01)

On EUR/USD, one pip on a standard lot is worth about **$10**, on a mini lot about $1, and on a micro lot about $0.10.

## Leverage
Leverage lets you control a large position with a small deposit (margin). With 1:100 leverage, $1,000 of margin controls $100,000. Leverage does not change how much a pip is worth — it changes how big a position you *can* open. That is exactly why it is dangerous: it makes oversized positions easy.

## The takeaway
Decide how much you are willing to lose first, then work out the lot size. Use the Position Size Calculator on this page for every trade.

lessons.title: The 1% rule: position sizing that keeps you alive
lessons.summary: Why professionals risk a small, fixed share of their account on every trade.
lessons.body:
## The rule
Risk no more than **1–2% of your account** on any single trade. On a $500 account, 1% is $5. That is the most you lose if your stop loss is hit.

## Why it works
Every strategy has losing streaks. Ten losses in a row at 1% risk leaves you with about 90% of your account. Ten losses at 10% risk leaves about 35%, and you now need a +187% gain just to get back to where you started.

## How to size a trade
- Decide your risk in money: balance × risk %
- Measure your stop loss in pips
- Lot size = risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)

Example: $1,000 balance, 1% risk = $10. Stop = 20 pips on EUR/USD ($10 per pip per standard lot). Lot size = 10 ÷ (20 × 10) = **0.05 lots**.

## The takeaway
Your stop loss decides where you are wrong; your position size decides how much being wrong costs. Never move the stop to fit a bigger lot.

lessons.title: Reading candlesticks without the mysticism
lessons.summary: What a candle actually tells you — and what it doesn't.
lessons.body:
## Anatomy
Each candle shows four prices for its time period: **open, high, low, close**. The body runs from open to close; the wicks show the high and low.

## What candles tell you
- A long body means one side controlled the period
- A long wick means price went somewhere and was rejected
- Small bodies with wicks on both sides mean indecision

## What they don't tell you
A single candle pattern is not a signal by itself. A hammer in the middle of nowhere means little; a hammer at a major support level after a sell-off, on a higher timeframe, means more.

## The takeaway
Read candles in context: **where** they form (key levels), **when** (session, news) and on **which timeframe**. Location first, pattern second.

lessons.title: Market structure: highs, lows and breaks
lessons.summary: The simplest way to read trend direction on any chart.
lessons.body:
## Uptrend, downtrend, range
- **Uptrend:** higher highs and higher lows
- **Downtrend:** lower highs and lower lows
- **Range:** price bouncing between a ceiling and a floor

## Break of structure
In an uptrend, a close below the last higher low is a warning that buyers are losing control. In a downtrend, a close above the last lower high is the warning for sellers.

## Using it
- Trade with the structure of the higher timeframe (for example 4H)
- Time entries on the lower timeframe (for example 15M)
- Put your stop beyond the swing point that would prove you wrong

## The takeaway
Structure gives you direction and a logical place for your stop. It doesn't predict the future — it tells you who is in control right now.

lessons.title: Binary options: your breakeven win rate
lessons.summary: One formula that shows why most binary traders lose.
lessons.body:
## The payout problem
A typical binary option pays **80–90%** of your stake on a win and loses **100%** on a loss. Wins pay less than losses cost.

## Breakeven win rate
Breakeven = 1 ÷ (1 + payout)
- 80% payout → 1 ÷ 1.80 = **55.6%**
- 85% payout → 1 ÷ 1.85 = **54.1%**
- 90% payout → 1 ÷ 1.90 = **52.6%**

Winning half your trades is not enough; at an 85% payout, a 50% win rate loses about 7.5% of everything you stake over time.

## Before you trade binaries
- Check the broker is licensed by a real regulator — many binary brokers are not
- Track at least 100 demo trades to measure your real win rate
- Set a hard daily loss limit and stop when you hit it

## The takeaway
Use the Binary Expectancy Calculator on this page. If your tracked win rate doesn't beat breakeven, the honest answer is not to trade.

lessons.title: Crypto security: seed phrases, wallets & scams
lessons.summary: The rules that protect your coins from the most common attacks.
lessons.body:
## Your seed phrase is your money
The 12 or 24 words of a wallet's seed phrase **are** the wallet. Anyone who has them can take everything.
- Write it on paper (or metal), never in a screenshot, email or cloud note
- No real support agent, exchange or developer will ever ask for it

## Wallet types
- **Exchange account:** convenient, but the exchange holds your coins
- **Software wallet:** you hold the keys on your phone or computer
- **Hardware wallet:** keys stay on a device offline — the best for long-term savings

## Common scams
- Fake support accounts replying to your posts
- "Account managers" who promise daily returns
- Airdrop links that ask you to connect and sign
- P2P buyers sending fake M-Pesa messages — always check your actual balance

## The takeaway
Slow down. Verify every address, every link and every person. In crypto, a mistake usually can't be reversed.

lessons.title: Choosing a broker: regulation first
lessons.summary: How to check a broker before you send it a shilling.
lessons.body:
## Check the licence
In Kenya, the **Capital Markets Authority (CMA)** licenses online forex brokers. Search the broker's name on the CMA's list of licensed market intermediaries. Other strong regulators include the FCA (UK) and ASIC (Australia).

## Red flags
- Bonuses that lock your withdrawals
- Guaranteed returns or "account management"
- Pressure to deposit more to unlock profits
- Support only through WhatsApp or Telegram

## Compare
- Spreads and commissions on the pairs you trade
- Deposit and withdrawal methods (M-Pesa, bank, card) and their fees
- How long withdrawals actually take — test with a small amount first

## The takeaway
A good strategy at a bad broker is still a bad trade. Verify first, deposit small, withdraw once, then decide.

lessons.title: Drawdowns and the maths of recovery
lessons.summary: Why losses hurt more than gains help.
lessons.body:
## The asymmetry
To recover from a loss you need a bigger percentage gain:
- −10% needs +11.1%
- −25% needs +33.3%
- −50% needs +100%
- −75% needs +300%

The formula: gain needed = loss ÷ (1 − loss).

## What it means
Avoiding big drawdowns matters more than chasing big wins. A strategy that makes 20% a year with a 10% worst drawdown is usually better than one that makes 60% with a 50% drawdown — because you can actually stick with it.

## Practical limits
- Daily loss limit: stop trading after −3%
- Weekly limit: reduce size after −6%
- Review everything after −10%

## The takeaway
Protect the account first. Use the Drawdown Recovery tool on this page to see what a loss really costs.

lessons.title: Trading psychology: rules over feelings
lessons.summary: The habits that separate consistent traders from gamblers.
lessons.body:
## Feelings are information, not instructions
Fear, greed and boredom show up in every trader. The goal isn't to stop feeling them; it's to have rules that decide for you.

## Rules that help
- Write your plan before the session, not during it
- One bad trade is allowed; revenge trading is not
- Fixed risk per trade — no exceptions after a loss
- Stop for the day after hitting your loss limit

## Keep a journal
Record the setup, entry, stop, target, result **and how you felt**. After 50 trades, patterns appear that no indicator will show you.

## The takeaway
Consistency comes from process. Download the Trading Journal Template and Pre-Trade Checklist on this page and use them every day.

qa.question: Can you build a website for my small business that takes M-Pesa payments?
qa.answer: Yes. The Commerce package covers online stores with M-Pesa and card checkout, and smaller sites can add a pay-with-M-Pesa button. Send me what you sell and roughly how many products, and I'll recommend the right setup.

qa.question: Do you trade or manage money on behalf of clients?
qa.answer: No. I teach, mentor and build tools. I don't hold or manage anyone's funds. If anyone claims to be me and offers account management, it's a scam — please report it using the official links on this site.

qa.question: How do partnership proposals work?
qa.answer: Send your proposal through the Connect panel. You'll get a reference code you can use to check its status. I review every proposal, and if it's a fit we set up a call to talk terms.

qa.question: I'm a complete beginner. Which course should I start with?
qa.answer: For tech, start with Web Development: Zero to Launch. For markets, start with Forex Foundations & Risk Management — it teaches the risk rules every other strategy depends on.

qa.question: What do you need from me to start a website?
qa.answer: Your business name, what you sell, three websites you like, your logo if you have one, and the main action you want visitors to take (call, buy, book or WhatsApp). I'll handle the rest.
